This code doesn't look right.  It should be doing something like

objectPath.parent() == path

Which was actually added to prevent this kind of bug.

We don't define namespaces separated by underscores, so I'd be fairly against this change, as it perpetuates "invented" namespaces in a subfield name.

https://github.com/openbmc/bmcweb/blob/master/docs/COMMON_ERRORS.md#12-imprecise-matching

Is the documentation bmcweb uses to justify this there.

Your idea does not solve the problem for me because it involves a behavior change.

Yes, most of the linked codes are probably not right to do it like that, but that does not mean we can just go ahead and change them easily without reviewing the surrounding code.

With this change we can easily replace the existing code and achieve better encapsulation of our string member.

It's an incremental upgrade for existing code, and there is no claim that it is the right solution long term.

Users of `object_path` can do whatever they like currently since the string member is public. So fixing that in the fastest way (without behavior change of user code) should be prioritized over ideal usage which is unrealistic given the current state of the codebase and review timelines for any patches that involve behavior changes.

Thanks for your feedback, i did add a comment to the header saying that this function should not be used for new code and `parent_path()` is the preferred choice.

> Your idea does not solve the problem for me because it involves a behavior change.
> 
> Yes, most of the linked codes are probably not right to do it like that, but that does not mean we can just go ahead and change them easily without reviewing the surrounding code.

I didn't suggest we change code without review or testing.

> 
> With this change we can easily replace the existing code and achieve better encapsulation of our string member.

I would strongly prefer we don't and just continue to fix the core of the problem.  Adding this to the library implies that there's a correct way to use it.

> 
> It's an incremental upgrade for existing code, and there is no claim that it is the right solution long term.

No argument there, my issue is this is actively going backward by adding an API that would be tough to remove later.

If your goal is to encapsulate the string internals, converting the code to using the existing parent/filename APIs would get you that result without needing this API.

> 
> Users of `object_path` can do whatever they like currently since the string member is public. So fixing that in the fastest way (without behavior change of user code) should be prioritized over ideal usage which is unrealistic given the current state of the codebase and review timelines for any patches that involve behavior changes.
> 
> Thanks for your feedback, i did add a comment to the header saying that this function should not be used for new code and `parent_path()` is the preferred choice.

I'm still against adding this API.  I know you linked 3 uses of starts_with, is that a complete list, or are there more?

There are at least 6 source locations involving `starts_with`

https://github.com/search?q=org%3Aopenbmc+.str.starts_with%28&type=code

and at least 4 source locations involving `substr`
https://github.com/search?q=org%3Aopenbmc+.str.substr&type=code

Then 7 problems involving `find`
https://github.com/search?q=org%3Aopenbmc+.str.find&type=code

And 2 issues involving `rfind`
https://github.com/search?q=org%3Aopenbmc+.str.rfind&type=code

One of those problems is in fw update code and was introduced by me, fix is already up https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/phosphor-bmc-code-mgmt/+/91192

Also, people are adding new usages of `object_path::str` member all the time. If you blame this one, that's an `rfind` which was added just last week.

https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-bmc-code-mgmt/blame/3b9435fc224cc46f2fa1248388d02e26e4d5c85c/common/src/events.cpp#L21

I am not saying someone cannot do an `rfind('_')` on an `object_path`, i just want to make this into an actual object path value type instead of just a fancy `std::string` wrapper.

If we just offer a fancy `std::string` wrapper to people then they might as well use `std::string`.


Keep in mind there might be yet more `std::string` APIs in use on our object path, you can look for yourself also.


> I didn't suggest we change code without review or testing.

It did not need testing when we did the `sdbusplus::message::object_path -> sdbusplus::object_path` migration. Not every change has to be tedious.

> There are at least 6 source locations involving `starts_with`
> 
> https://github.com/search?q=org%3Aopenbmc+.str.starts_with%28&type=code

The 3 left in bmcweb I'm aware of.  The ethernet PATCH one is very non trivial to test and get right (we've broken it several times in the last year and phosphor-network supports two variations) so I haven't had a desire to touch it.

I do see there might be a use case for an "is_child_of()" method in some of them.  That would let you do

if ({"/xyz/openbmc_project/foo/bar"}.is_child_of("/xyz/openbmc_project")

That wouldn't violate the "starts_with" rules, but would still let you do a similar test?

> 
> and at least 4 source locations involving `substr`
> https://github.com/search?q=org%3Aopenbmc+.str.substr&type=code
> 
> Then 7 problems involving `find`
> https://github.com/search?q=org%3Aopenbmc+.str.find&type=code
> 
> And 2 issues involving `rfind`
> https://github.com/search?q=org%3Aopenbmc+.str.rfind&type=code
> 
> One of those problems is in fw update code and was introduced by me, fix is already up https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/phosphor-bmc-code-mgmt/+/91192

Thank you for this.

> 
> Also, people are adding new usages of `object_path::str` member all the time. If you blame this one, that's an `rfind` which was added just last week.
> 
> https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-bmc-code-mgmt/blame/3b9435fc224cc46f2fa1248388d02e26e4d5c85c/common/src/events.cpp#L21
> 
> I am not saying someone cannot do an `rfind('_')` on an `object_path`, i just want to make this into an actual object path value type instead of just a fancy `std::string` wrapper.

That one doesn't suffer from the error I described above, but arguably should be

path.filename().rfind(...) to avoid going to the string internals.

> 
> If we just offer a fancy `std::string` wrapper to people then they might as well use `std::string`.

object_path has escaping and concatenation primitives like std::filesystem::path.  In a lot of cases, it replaced people trying to use std::filesystem::path for dbus construction.  I agree, I don't like that the string is accessible, but it was necessary for a lot of cases.

> 
> 
> Keep in mind there might be yet more `std::string` APIs in use on our object path, you can look for yourself also.
> 
> 
> > I didn't suggest we change code without review or testing.
> 
> It did not need testing when we did the `sdbusplus::message::object_path -> sdbusplus::object_path` migration. Not every change has to be tedious.

I'm not sure how a simple rename of namespace is similar to calling different code, but that's not important to this patch.
Overall not in support of this change.  The linked code looks incorrect and needs fixed.

The linked code is responsibility of the respective maintainers, and they will determine if it needs fixed.

I would appreciate if you could fix the issue on bmcweb side.

sdbusplus can only provide the `object_path` API, whoever writes the user code will determine how they want to use it.

What we can do in sdbusplus is provide a better way to do what the user code is already doing.
In this case the improvement is that the string member is not accessed directly.

We don't have any disagreement that the linked code is probably wrong.

> I would appreciate if you could fix the issue on bmcweb side.

I've been working on fixing the overall issue for years and fixed a lot of the issues already.  It's just not the highest priority for me.  I would prefer we don't make the problem worse by adding library APIs.

> We don't have any disagreement that the linked code is probably wrong.

Awesome.  My strong preference is that we just fix the wrong code.  I understand that requires testing, but that's ok.

> I've been working on fixing the overall issue for years and fixed a lot of the issues already. 

Are you sure the issue did not get worse or stay the same over time?

There is a lot of repos and a lot of people adding new code, so even if you make progress in your corner, the project as a whole may still regress.

> Awesome.  My strong preference is that we just fix the wrong code.  I understand that requires testing, but that's ok.

Well if you spent years trying to fix it and it did not get fixed, maybe your way of fixing it is not working?

My proposed solution:

- figure out which std::string APIs are used on object_path (e.g. `starts_with`)
- provide those APIs on top of `object_path`, even if they are 'wrong'. we can just document them as such.

- merge changes to use those directly instead of `object_path::str` member access
- not do any testing on those changes
- make `object_path::str` private
- migrate users to better APIs (may require testing)

That puts sdbusplus maintainers back in control on how `object_path` can be used instead of exposing the whole `std::string` surface on a mutable member variable.
Thanks for reviewing so quickly 👍
